title: Cinematic Post-Processing Director Suite
description: The user acts as a cinematic director composing a dramatic scene where a chess set from ABeautifulGame sits atop a reflective surface beside a ShaderBall2 used as a material/lighting reference. A panel of post-processing controls lets the user layer and fine-tune bloom, depth of field, chromatic aberration, vignette, color grading, and film grain to craft a final cinematic look, with a screenshot capture button to save the result.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with ES module imports from cdn.jsdelivr.net including three, OrbitControls, GLTFLoader, EffectComposer, RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, ShaderPass, and GammaCorrectionShader. Load ShaderBall2.glb and place it on the left side of the scene at position (-2, 0, 0). Load ABeautifulGame.glb (a chess set) and place it on the right side at position (2, 0, 0). Add a reflective ground plane using MeshStandardMaterial with metalness 0.9 and roughness 0.1 beneath both models. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 7) looking at the origin. Add a warm DirectionalLight, a cool-toned HemisphereLight, and a subtle RectAreaLight for cinematic fill. Build an EffectComposer with RenderPass and UnrealBloomPass. Add custom ShaderPasses for: (1) depth-of-field with adjustable focus distance and aperture, (2) chromatic aberration with adjustable offset, (3) vignette with adjustable intensity and softness, (4) color grading with adjustable lift/gamma/gain RGB values, and (5) film grain with adjustable intensity. Create an HTML/CSS overlay panel on the right side with labeled sliders for these parameters: Bloom Threshold (0-1, default 0.8), Bloom Strength (0-3, default 1.5), Bloom Radius (0-1, default 0.4), DOF Focus Distance (1-15, default 5), DOF Aperture (0.001-0.05, default 0.01), Chromatic Aberration Offset (0-0.01, default 0.002), Vignette Intensity (0-1.5, default 0.7), Vignette Softness (0-1, default 0.5), Color Grading Warmth (-1 to 1, default 0.1), and Film Grain Intensity (0-0.5, default 0.1). Each slider must update its corresponding uniform in real time. Validate all parameters stay within their defined ranges. Add a toggle button to show a split-screen before/after comparison where the left half renders without post-processing and the right half with all effects applied. Add a capture button that uses renderer.domElement.toDataURL to save a screenshot. Include OrbitControls for camera manipulation. The scene background should be a dark gradient environment. Animate a subtle rotation on the ShaderBall2 model to showcase material response to the post-processing effects.
